candidate_positive: verdict exactly FINDING; UNCERTAIN is counted separately and is not a positive

matching.eligibility: A FINDING candidate is eligible for a reference defect iff claim_type is accepted and its exact target_span code-point interval overlaps any registered localization-anchor occurrence.
matching.assignment: Per item, choose maximum-cardinality one-to-one candidate/reference matching; ties use lexicographically smallest candidate-index/reference-id pair sequence.
matching.multiple_defects: Each sealed natural defect is a separate reference denominator and one candidate can match at most one defect.
matching.correction_acceptability: For a matched candidate, replace each exact occurrence of target_span in turn; acceptable iff any resulting full target exactly equals a preregistered acceptable_full_targets string.
matching.localization_acceptability: Numerator: FINDING candidates on defective items eligible under the overlap rule. Denominator: all FINDING candidates on defective items only. Clean-item false positives affect precision/specificity but are not double-penalized here.

balanced_accuracy: mean(defective-item sensitivity, clean-item specificity); defective item sensitivity counts an item detected when at least one reference defect is matched
union: For each dataset/condition, union all FINDING candidates from the three runs, deduplicated by canonical candidate tuple, then score once; descriptive derived result.
consensus: For each dataset/condition, retain canonical candidate tuples appearing in at least two of three runs, then score once; descriptive derived result.
null_rule: Any zero denominator is null, never zero. Zero candidates remain a valid effectiveness outcome.
headline_rule: Never pool H1 and H2. Report all three measured runs before descriptive union/consensus.

structural_not_measured.registered_evidence_field: Exact evidence vs evidence_quote conformance is enforced by strict schema/parser acceptance and is not reported as a candidate-level metric.
